the-open-air: Richard Jefferies — the great English nature writer — celebrates the open air in these luminous essays on fields, birds, and seasons. His prose glows with a rare and intense beauty. A classic of nature writing that has never lost its freshness.
the-poetical-works-of-henry-kirk-white-w: Henry Kirke White, the Nottingham prodigy who died at twenty-one, left poems of remarkable promise — gathered here with Southey's memoir. His melancholy genius touched Byron and all England. A moving monument to unfulfilled promise. consumption took him young, but his verses on hope and melancholy still move tender readers.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: The Iron Gate and Other Poems faces age and loss with Holmes' characteristic courage, humor, and faith. His later verse has an autumnal beauty all its own — tender without self-pity. The poet grown old gracefully, and greatly. Courage and kindness meet old age hand in hand.
ars-recte-vivendi-being-essays-contribut: George William Curtis' Easy Chair essays on the art of right living — manners, morals, books, and the good life — graced Harper's Magazine for years. His urbane, humane wisdom made him America's beloved mentor. The classic American essay at its most civilized.
the-dialect-of-the-west-of-england-parti: James Jennings records the dialect of the West of England, particularly Somersetshire — its words, sayings, and grammar, gathered with loving care. His pioneering glossary preserves a fading rural speech. Precious to philologists and to all lovers of old England. Zummerzet voices sound again in his faithful record.
